name: coordinator-claim-consistency-check
body:
After a writer returns an ACTIONED or WONT-FIX claim, the coordinator performs a quick, shallow consistency check of the claim — not a deep correctness review — and then actions the item or re-dispatches it. Examples of the check: a claim of ACTIONED with no change made, or a claim of WONT-FIX that did make changes, is an inconsistency to re-dispatch; a claim consistent with the observed change is actioned. Once consistent, the coordinator marks the item actioned with the claimed disposition (`apg review action <f> --fix|--wont-fix`); the reviewer then resolves (terminal) or rejects (reopen). The coordinator repeats the dispatch/claim/check loop until all feedback is addressed.

Acceptance: the coordinator's check compares the claim against the actual change (ACTIONED ⇒ change present; WONT-FIX ⇒ no change or only unrelated change) and never decides correctness; an inconsistent claim is re-dispatched rather than actioned; a consistent claim is actioned; the coordinator never resolves or rejects — that stays the reviewer's terminal act.
